items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction, and the first appearance of the exact compound is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：日耳曼语之前的词根属重构形式，这一确切复合词的首见年代亦不确定。

note.en: Group one holds expressions built on the same process word or the same learning family; group two holds terms for study seen from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「过程」一词或「学习」词族的说法；第二组是从别的角度看学习的说法。

entries.definition: A plotted line of progress over time; it names a measurement of the process, not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间画出的进度曲线；它命名的是对过程的测量，而非过程本身。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb for going forward, but it names an established way of doing a task, not how a mind learns.
entries.definitionCN: 同出表示「向前走」的拉丁动词，但它指做某事的既定方式，而非心智如何学习。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning 'to go on'; it describes movement, not acquisition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，意为「继续进行」；它描述移动，而非获取。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb meaning 'to read'; a lesson is one unit of teaching, not the whole sequence of learning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「读」的拉丁动词；一课是一个教学单元，不是整个学习序列。

entries.definition: The knowledge gained or the activity in general; the process word emphasises order and stages.
entries.definitionCN: 获得的知识或一般性的活动；过程一词强调顺序与阶段。

entries.definition: The gaining of a skill or language, often used in research; it names the outcome more than the steps.
entries.definitionCN: 技能或语言的获得，多用于研究语境；它更命名结果而非步骤。

entries.definition: Deliberate effort to learn, especially by reading; it names the work, not the whole developmental sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 为学习付出的刻意努力，尤指阅读；它命名这份工作，而非整个发展序列。

entries.definition: Structured practice for a skill or job; it is a narrower, usually external, form of learning.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项技能或工作安排的结构化练习；它是较窄、通常由外部安排的学习形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the track image in learn, the advance image in process, and the school phrases that use both.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「学习」的词里的「轨迹」意象、表示「过程」的词里的「推进」意象，以及同时用到两者的学校说法。

normal.en: Learn once meant following a track, and process means going forward, so the phrase is a walk along a path.
normal.cn: 表示「学习」的词曾经指沿轨迹走，表示「过程」的词意为向前推进，所以这个短语就是沿路行走。

normal.en: The phrase always implies order: first exposure, then practice, then independence.
normal.cn: 这个短语总含顺序：先接触，再练习，最后独立。

normal.en: School phrases mark the term: the learning process, support the learning process, learning process assessment.
normal.cn: 学校的固定说法标出这个术语：学习过程、支持学习过程、学习过程评估。

normal.en: If you can draw progress as a line, you are measuring the process rather than living it.
normal.cn: 如果你能把进度画成一条线，你是在测量过程，而不是在经历它。

normal.en: Organisations use the same phrase for teams, which shows how easily the idea scales from one mind to many.
normal.cn: 组织把同一短语用在团队上，可见这一想法多容易从一个人扩展到许多人。

abstract.en: Picture footprints appearing one after another on wet sand.
abstract.cn: 想象湿沙上出现一个接一个的脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge built plank by plank before anyone crosses.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥在有人过河之前被一块块板铺好。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph developing slowly in a tray of liquid.
abstract.cn: 想象一张照片在显影液里慢慢显现。

examples.en: The learning process slowed whenever feedback arrived too late.
examples.cn: 每当反馈来得太晚，学习过程就慢下来。

examples.en: Textbooks often hide the learning process by printing only the right answer.
examples.cn: 教科书只印正确答案，往往把学习过程藏了起来。

examples.en: Her learning process involved three drafts and two failed experiments.
examples.cn: 她的学习过程包括三稿和两次失败的实验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「学一段、进一步」——沿着路一步步往前走，就是学习过程

root: 表示「学习」的本族动词来自古英语「获得知识、沿轨迹走」，深层词根表「轨迹」；表示「过程」的名词来自拉丁语「向前推进」，由「向前」加「走」构成。两词合指按顺序推进的学习历程。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a single path: a learner moving from first contact to confident use. The path is then examined as stages, as mental operations, as classroom design, as adult experience, as group routine and as an object of assessment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一条路径展开：学习者从初次接触到熟练运用。这条路径随后被分别看成阶段、心智活动、课堂设计、成人经验、群体惯例与评估对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footprints appearing one after another along a path, including the ones that went wrong.
core.cn: 核心意象：小路上一个接一个出现的脚印，包括走错的那几个。

branches.en: FROM START TO MASTERY: the longest reading, the full ladder from ignorance to fluency.
branches.cn: 从起点到熟练：最长的读法，从不知到流畅的整架梯子。

branches.en: INSIDE THE HEAD: attention and memory are the machinery that moves the learner along.
branches.cn: 头脑内部：注意与记忆是推动学习者前进的机构。

branches.en: DESIGNED ORDER: classrooms and textbooks arrange the path in advance so it can be repeated.
branches.cn: 被设计的顺序：课堂与教科书预先排好路径，使它可重复。

branches.en: THE ADULT PATH: experience changes which steps come first.
branches.cn: 成人的路径：经验改变了哪些步骤先走。

branches.en: THE PATH JUDGED AND SHARED: teams walk it together, and assessors watch how it is walked.
branches.cn: 被评判与共享的路径：团队一起走，评估者则看它怎么走。

intro.en: The phrase joins a native verb to a Latin noun; both parts are common enough to be read separately and then together.
intro.cn: 这个短语把本族动词与拉丁名词连在一起；两部分都足够常见，可以先分开读，再合起来读。

latinIntro.en: The learning part is Old English and needs no Latin; the process part is Latin 'a going forward', with a prefix and a verb inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 「学习」这一半是古英语，不需拉丁语解释；「过程」这一半是拉丁语「前进」，内部还含一个前缀和一个动词。

items.meaning: a going forward; a series of steps

items.example: The class proceeded to the next unit.
The safety procedure was posted on the wall.

definition_zh: 知识；学识；了解，知悉；技能，熟练；认识（对某人或某地的熟悉）
definition_en: the facts, information and understanding that a person has acquired, or the state of being aware of something
core_image: 老木匠不看图纸，手指一摸榫头就知道差了几分
scene: 老木匠不看图纸，手指一摸就知道榫头差了几分。His knowledge of joinery came from forty years at the bench, not from a book.
sceneCN: 这里 knowledge 指「通过长期实践积累起来的理解与熟练」（第 1 个义项：知识与理解的整体）；句意为他对榫卯的了解来自四十年的工作台，而非书本。可辨识物件：工作台、刨子、榫头、木屑。

pos.zh: 知识；学识；了解，知悉；技能，熟练；（对某人某地的）熟悉

senses.title: The body of what is known
senses.definition: the facts, information and understanding a person or a field has acquired
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一个领域所获得的事实、信息与理解
senses.example: His knowledge of joinery came from forty years at the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 他对榫卯的了解来自四十年的工作台。
senses.why: The noun names the whole store of what has been learned, not one item in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名所学之物的全部储藏，而不是其中一项。

senses.title: Understanding from experience
senses.definition: a working grasp of how something behaves, gained by doing rather than by reading
senses.definitionCN: 通过做而非通过读所获得的、关于事物如何运作的实用把握
senses.example: Her knowledge of the river told her where the current would turn.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这条河的认识告诉她水流会在哪里转向。
senses.why: Experience supplies a kind of knowing that facts alone cannot, and the word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 经验提供一种单靠事实得不到的知，这个词覆盖了它。

senses.title: Skill and competence
senses.definition: the practical ability to do something well, as in a craft or a trade
senses.definitionCN: 把某事做好的实际能力，如某项手艺或行业
senses.example: He has some knowledge of plumbing.
senses.exampleCN: 他会一些管道工的活。
senses.why: In older English knowing a trade and being able to do it were the same claim.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的英语里，懂一门手艺与会做这门手艺是同一个说法。

senses.title: Awareness of a fact
senses.definition: the state of being aware that something is true or has happened
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事为真或已发生的状态
senses.example: The knowledge that the letter had arrived changed her plans.
senses.exampleCN: 知道那封信已寄到，改变了她的计划。
senses.why: Knowing that something is so requires no expertise, only information, so the word reaches this low bar too.
senses.whyCN: 知道某事如此并不需要专门学问，只需信息，这个词也覆盖这一低门槛。

senses.title: Familiarity with a person or place
senses.definition: acquaintance with someone or somewhere, from repeated contact
senses.definitionCN: 因反复接触而对某人或某地产生的熟识
senses.example: The guide's knowledge of the old quarter saved us an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 向导对老城区的熟悉替我们省了一小时。
senses.why: Repeated contact builds a mental map, and the same noun names that map.
senses.whyCN: 反复接触会建立一张心智地图，同一个名词命名这张地图。

senses.title: Scholarly learning
senses.definition: the accumulated learning of a discipline or of a learned person
senses.definitionCN: 一个学科或一位博学之人所积累的学问
senses.example: The library is the visible form of the university's knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆是这所大学学识的可见形态。
senses.why: Institutions store knowledge outside any single head, and the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 机构把知识存放在任何单个头脑之外，这个词也跟着到了那里。

senses.title: Tacit knowledge
senses.definition: knowledge a person can use but finds hard to put into words
senses.definitionCN: 一个人会用却难以说清的知识
senses.example: The potter's tacit knowledge showed in the even glaze.
senses.exampleCN: 陶工的默会知识体现在均匀的釉面上。
senses.why: Some knowing lives in the hands, and theorists needed a separate label for it.
senses.whyCN: 有些知存在于双手之中，理论家因此需要另立一个标签。

senses.title: Justified true belief
senses.titleCN: 有正当理由的真实信念
senses.definition: in philosophy, a belief that is true and supported by adequate reasons
senses.definitionCN: 哲学用语：为真且有充分理由支持的信念
senses.example: The seminar asked whether knowledge differs from lucky guessing.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课追问知识与侥幸猜中是否有别。
senses.why: Philosophy narrows the everyday word to a strict condition, which is why it needs its own definition.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常词收窄为一个严格条件，因此需要自己的定义。

intro.en: Knowledge descends from an Old English verb for knowing, with a Middle English noun ending whose history is partly obscure. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: knowledge 源自古英语表示「知道」的动词，带一个中古英语名词词尾，该词尾的来历部分不清楚。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cnāwan meant 'to know, recognise, perceive'; its Indo-European ancestor is reconstructed with an initial consonant cluster typical of the knowing root.
items.cn: 这个古英语动词意为「知道、认出、察觉」；其印欧祖形被重构，带有「知」这一词根常见的首辅音组合。

items.en: The verb knowlechen meant 'to acknowledge, confess, recognise', and from it a noun for the state of knowing developed.
items.cn: 中古英语动词意为「承认、告白、认出」，由它发展出表示「知的状态」的名词。

items.en: The ending of knowledge matches the one in acknowledgement; its exact origin is debated and is marked as source uncertain.
items.cn: knowledge 的词尾与表示「承认」的那个词的词尾一致；其确切来源有争议，标为来源不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth century knowledge was the standard spelling for learning and awareness, and the older verb sense faded.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这一拼写已成表示学识与知悉的标准形式，较古的动词义则消退。

items.en: Philosophers later fixed a technical sense, justified true belief, alongside the everyday senses.
items.cn: 哲学家后来在日常义之外固定了一个技术义：有正当理由的真实信念。

items.en: Source uncertain (suffix origin): the noun ending cannot be derived with certainty, and the reconstructed Indo-European root is not attested in any text.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词尾来源）：这一名词词尾无法确定地推导出来，重构的印欧词根也没有任何文本书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same knowing root or easily mistaken for it; group two holds the near synonyms that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「知」这一词根、或容易被误认的词；第二组是范围有别的近义词。

entries.definition: Built on the same knowing stem, but its prefix adds the sense of admitting or confirming, not possessing facts.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「知」这一词干，但前缀增添了「承认、确认」的意思，而非拥有事实。

entries.definition: The verb states the act of knowing; knowledge is the noun for what is held or the state of holding it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词陈述「知道」这一动作；knowledge 是名词，指所持之物或持有的状态。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb meaning 'to make known', a different family; it means to observe something, not to possess understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「使知晓」的拉丁动词，属另一词族；它指注意到某物，而非拥有理解。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb meaning 'to know again'; it stresses identifying something met before, not the store of learning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「再次知道」的拉丁动词；它强调认出先前见过之物，而非学问的储藏。

entries.definition: Facts supplied or stored; information becomes knowledge when a person understands and can use it.
entries.definitionCN: 被提供或储存的事实；信息被人理解并能使用时，才成为知识。

entries.definition: A grasp of how facts fit together; knowledge can be a list, understanding is the pattern in it.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实如何相互契合的把握；知识可以是清单，理解则是清单中的格局。

entries.definition: Advanced skill and knowledge in a narrow field, usually demonstrated in performance.
entries.definitionCN: 在狭窄领域内的高水平技能与知识，通常通过实际表现来证明。

entries.definition: The activity of acquiring knowledge or the scholarship that results; knowledge is the content itself.
entries.definitionCN: 获取知识的活动或由此形成的学问；knowledge 是内容本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the knowing root, the fixed phrases, and the contrast between information and understanding.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「知」这一词根、固定说法，以及信息与理解之间的对比。

normal.en: The word is built on an old verb for knowing, so it names the content of knowing rather than the act.
normal.cn: 这个词建立在表示「知道」的古动词上，因此命名的是所知的内容，而非动作。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: general knowledge, knowledge of a subject, to my knowledge.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：常识、对某学科的掌握、据我所知。

normal.en: Knowledge can be held by a person, a library or a company; the noun does not require a mind.
normal.cn: 知识可以由一个人、一座图书馆或一家公司持有；这个名词不要求有一个头脑。

normal.en: Tacit knowledge is real knowledge that resists being written down, which is why apprenticeships still exist.
normal.cn: 默会知识是真实存在却难以写下的知识，这就是师徒制仍然存在的原因。

normal.en: Acknowledging something is not the same as knowing it; the shared stem hides a difference in prefix.
normal.cn: 承认某事与知道某事并不相同；共同的词干掩盖了前缀带来的差别。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf that grows heavier without anyone seeing the books arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架越来越重，却没人看见书是什么时候到的。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn in the head by walking the same street many times.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在地图册之外、靠反复走同一条街画在头脑里的地图。

abstract.en: Picture light passing through a window into a room that was already full.
abstract.cn: 想象光穿过窗户照进一间本就装满东西的屋子。

examples.en: The report turns scattered data into usable knowledge.
examples.cn: 这份报告把零散的数据变成可用的知识。

examples.en: To my knowledge, nobody has repeated the experiment.
examples.cn: 据我所知，还没有人重复过这个实验。

examples.en: Local knowledge of the tides mattered more than the map.
examples.cn: 对当地潮汐的了解比地图更要紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脑子里的存货」——知道的东西越攒越多 → 知识

root: 古英语动词「知道、认出、察觉」加中古英语名词词尾，构成「所知之物」；词尾来源不确定，其印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one store: what a mind or an institution holds and can use. The store is counted as facts, as experience, as skill, as awareness, as familiarity, as scholarship, as silent craft and finally as a philosopher's strict condition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个储藏展开：一个头脑或一个机构所持有并能使用的东西。这份储藏被分别算作事实、经验、技能、知悉、熟悉、学问、沉默的手艺，最后是哲学家设定的严格条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a store that grows without being displayed, and can be drawn on when needed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份不摆出来却不断增长的储藏，需要时能取用。

branches.en: THE STORE: what a person or a discipline keeps, whether in one head or in a library.
branches.cn: 储藏：一个人或一个学科保存之物，无论在头脑里还是在图书馆里。

branches.en: THE GRASP: experience turns stored facts into a working sense of how things behave.
branches.cn: 把握：经验把储存的事实变成对事物如何运作的实用感觉。

branches.en: THE HANDS: craft skill and tacit knowledge live in practice and resist full description.
branches.cn: 双手：手艺与默会知识活在实践里，难以被完全描述。

branches.en: THE LIGHT TOUCH: knowing a fact or a person needs contact, not expertise.
branches.cn: 轻触：知道一个事实或熟悉一个人只需接触，不需专门学问。

branches.en: THE NARROW GATE: philosophy asks what would make a belief count as knowledge at all.
branches.cn: 窄门：哲学追问究竟是什么让一个信念算得上知识。

intro.en: Knowledge is a native noun with an opaque ending; the useful units are the knowing stem and the endings it takes in related words.
intro.cn: knowledge 是本族名词，词尾理据不透明；有用的单位是「知」这一词干，以及相关词所带的词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source in this word, although the knowing root has distant Indo-European relatives. The ending is English and partly unexplained.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不含拉丁语来源，尽管「知」这一词根有遥远的印欧同族。词尾是英语的，且部分无法解释。

items.example: The ending also appears in acknowledgement.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾也出现在 acknowledgement 中。

items.example: A knowledgeable guide led the tour.
items.exampleCN: 一位在行的向导带队参观。

items.example: A known expert reviewed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 一位知名专家审阅了该计划。

items.example: The team built a knowledge base.

definition_zh: 知识渊博的；在行的，内行的；显示出知识的
definition_en: having a lot of information or understanding about a subject, and able to use it well
core_image: 集市上一个摊主抬头就能指出哪家铺子的秤最准，问的人还没说完
scene: 集市上，游客问哪家铺子的秤最准，摊主一句话就指对了人。The stallholder was knowledgeable about every supplier in the market.
sceneCN: 这里 knowledgeable 指「对某一范围了解很多且说得准」（第 1 个义项：见闻广博）；句意为这位摊主对市场里每个供货商都很在行。可辨识物件：摊位、秤、菜筐、手写的价牌。

pos.zh: 知识渊博的；在行的，内行的；显示出知识的

senses.title: Well informed in general
senses.definition: having a wide store of information and being able to draw on it
senses.definitionCN: 拥有广博的信息储备并能随时取用
senses.example: The stallholder was knowledgeable about every supplier in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这位摊主对市场里每个供货商都很在行。
senses.why: The suffix means 'having the quality', so the adjective says a person is full of what has been learned.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀意为「具有这种性质」，因此形容词表示一个人装满了所学之物。

senses.title: Expert in a field
senses.definition: possessing deep and reliable understanding of one subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题拥有深厚而可靠的理解
senses.example: She is knowledgeable about medieval tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 她精通中世纪税收档案。
senses.why: Depth, not breadth, is what separates an expert from someone merely well informed.
senses.whyCN: 是深度而非广度，把行家与仅仅见闻广的人区分开来。

senses.title: Showing knowledge
senses.definition: of an answer, question or remark, revealing that the speaker knows the subject
senses.definitionCN: 指回答、提问或言论显出说话者懂行
senses.example: He asked a knowledgeable question about the second clause.
senses.exampleCN: 他就第二条款提了一个很内行的问题。
senses.why: The adjective can describe the product of knowledge as well as the person who holds it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能描述知识的产物，也能描述持有知识的人。

senses.title: Well versed in a subject
senses.definition: familiar with the details and conventions of a field
senses.definitionCN: 熟悉某一领域的细节与惯例
senses.example: The technician was knowledgeable in electrical safety codes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位技术员熟悉电气安全规范。
senses.why: Familiarity with rules and details is a distinct kind of knowing, so the adjective takes 'in'.
senses.whyCN: 熟悉规则与细节是另一种知，因此这个形容词常接「在……方面」。

senses.title: Worth asking
senses.definition: of a person, reliable enough that others go to them for answers
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人可靠到别人会去找他求证
senses.example: For anything about the harbour, he is the knowledgeable one.
senses.exampleCN: 凡是关于港口的事，他才是懂行的那位。
senses.why: Knowledge becomes social when others route their questions through one person.
senses.whyCN: 当别人把问题都转给某一个人时，知识就变成了社会性的。

senses.title: A specialist audience
senses.definition: of a group, already carrying the background needed to follow a technical talk
senses.definitionCN: 指一群已具备听懂专业报告所需背景的人
senses.example: The lecture was aimed at a knowledgeable audience.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座面向有专业背景的听众。
senses.why: The adjective also measures the listener's store, not only the speaker's.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也衡量听者的储备，而不只是说话者的。

senses.title: Technically competent
senses.definition: having enough technical or legal knowledge to act correctly
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够的技术或法律知识以正确行事
senses.example: Only a knowledgeable operator should reset the valve.
senses.exampleCN: 只有懂行的操作员才该复位这个阀门。
senses.why: In technical settings, being knowledgeable is a safety requirement rather than a compliment.
senses.whyCN: 在技术场景里，懂行是安全要求，而不只是一句称赞。

senses.title: Carrying local knowledge
senses.definition: having the practical knowledge of a place that residents acquire
senses.definitionCN: 拥有居民才有的、关于某地的实用知识
senses.example: A knowledgeable neighbour warned us about the tide.
senses.exampleCN: 一位了解当地情况的邻居提醒我们注意潮水。
senses.why: Local knowledge is learned by living somewhere, which is why the adjective often describes guides and residents.
senses.whyCN: 当地情况靠住在那里学来，所以这个形容词常描述向导与居民。

intro.en: Knowledgeable is knowledge plus an English suffix meaning 'having the quality of'. The date is approximate.
intro.cn: knowledgeable 是表示「知识」的名词加一个表示「具有……性质」的英语后缀。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun for what is known supplies the whole stem, including its partly unexplained ending.
items.cn: 表示「所知之物」的名词提供整个词干，包括那个部分无法解释的词尾。

items.en: The suffix usually means 'able to be', but with nouns such as comfort or knowledge it means 'having the quality of'.
items.cn: 这个后缀通常表示「能够被」，但与表示安慰或知识的名词结合时，表示「具有……性质」。

items.en: The adjective is recorded from the early nineteenth century, when reviews needed a word for a well-stocked mind.
items.cn: 这个形容词自十九世纪初有记录，当时评论需要一个词来形容头脑充实的人。

items.en: It now appears mostly before nouns such as staff, audience, guide and operator, and after the preposition about.
items.cn: 它如今多出现在员工、听众、向导、操作员这类名词之前，以及「关于」这一介词之后。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest written use is not firmly dated, and the noun's own ending remains unexplained.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的书面用法年代不确，名词本身的词尾也仍无解释。

note.en: Group one holds words formed from the same knowing stem; group two holds the adjectives of competence it is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「知」词干的词；第二组是常与之混淆、表示能力的形容词。

entries.definition: Built on the same stem but with the passive sense, so it means 'able to be known', not 'full of knowledge'.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这一词干，但取被动义，意为「可被知道的」，而非「装满知识的」。

entries.definition: From the verb meaning 'to admit'; an acknowledged expert is recognised by others, which is a different claim.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「承认」的动词；「公认的」专家是被他人认可，这是另一种说法。

entries.definition: A compound describing an industry or system founded on information, not a person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，描述以信息为基础的行业或系统，而非持有信息的人。

entries.definition: Known by many people; fame says nothing about how much the person actually understands.
entries.definitionCN: 被许多人知道；名气并不说明此人实际懂多少。

entries.definition: Supplied with current facts, often about events; it stresses information rather than deep understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 掌握当前事实，常指时事；它强调信息而非深层理解。

entries.definition: Having special skill or knowledge in a field, usually certified by training or reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 在某领域有专门技能或知识，通常由训练或声誉证明。

entries.definition: Experienced and familiar with a subject's details, often used with 'in'.
entries.definitionCN: 有经验并熟悉某学科的细节，常与「在……方面」连用。

entries.definition: Having noticed something; awareness is far weaker than being knowledgeable.
entries.definitionCN: 已经注意到某事；知悉远比「在行」要弱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the noun stem, the suffix, and the prepositions that reveal the sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：名词词干、后缀，以及揭示词义的介词搭配。

normal.en: Knowledge plus a suffix meaning 'having the quality' equals a person full of it.
normal.cn: 表示「知识」的名词加上表示「具有这种性质」的后缀，等于一个装满知识的人。

normal.en: The preposition matters: knowledgeable about a subject, knowledgeable in a field.
normal.cn: 介词很要紧：对某主题在行，在某领域有专门知识。

normal.en: It usually describes people and their products: staff, guides, audiences and answers can all be knowledgeable.
normal.cn: 它通常描述人及其产物：员工、向导、听众与回答都可以是「内行的」。

normal.en: Compare knowable, which looks similar but means 'can be known', the opposite direction.
normal.cn: 对比表示「可被知道」的那个词：形似，却方向正相反。

normal.en: Being knowledgeable is a compliment; being expert is a credential; being informed is merely current.
normal.cn: 「在行」是称赞，「专家」是资历，「知情」只是掌握了近况。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer that opens without a search.
abstract.cn: 想象一个抽屉，不用翻找就能打开。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lights the whole room rather than one corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮整间屋子，而不只是一个角落。

abstract.en: Picture a map already folded into the right page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图早已翻到正确的那一页。

examples.en: The staff were knowledgeable and answered every question.
examples.cn: 员工很内行，回答了每个问题。

examples.en: A knowledgeable reader will notice the missing citation.
examples.cn: 内行的读者会注意到缺失的引注。

examples.en: He was knowledgeable about the river but not about the roads.
examples.cn: 他熟悉这条河，却不熟路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脑子里有货」——一开口就显出懂行 → 知识渊博的

root: knowledge（知识，古英语「知道」加名词词尾）+ 英语中表示「具有……性质」的后缀；英语 knowledgeable 指知识渊博、在行的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one well-stocked mind: full in general, deep in one field, visible in what the person says, familiar with details, worth consulting, present in an audience, reliable in technical matters and rooted in local experience.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一种充实的头脑：整体上见闻广、在某一领域有深度、从言谈中看得出来、熟悉细节、值得请教、也能出现在听众身上、在技术事务上可靠，并扎根于当地经验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawer that opens on the right answer without a search.
core.cn: 核心意象：一拉开就取出正确答案的抽屉。

branches.en: BREADTH: the adjective first says the store is large, without saying where it came from.
branches.cn: 广度：这个形容词首先说明储藏很大，却不说它从何而来。

branches.en: DEPTH: one field known down to its conventions, marked by the preposition 'in'.
branches.cn: 深度：某一领域连惯例都熟悉，由介词「在……方面」标出。

branches.en: WHAT OTHERS HEAR: a question or a lecture can show knowledge in the asker or the listener.
branches.cn: 别人听见的：一个提问或一场讲座，能在提问者或听者身上显出知识。

branches.en: THE PERSON OTHERS ROUTE QUESTIONS TO: knowledge becomes social when it is consulted.
branches.cn: 别人绕过去请教的人：知识在被请教时变成社会性的。

branches.en: RELIABILITY IN PLACE: technical safety and local tides both require knowing that a book cannot supply.
branches.cn: 在具体处境中的可靠：技术安全与当地潮汐都需要书本给不了的知。

intro.en: Knowledgeable is a two-piece English formation, and the same suffix behaves differently on nouns and on verbs.
intro.cn: knowledgeable 是两段式英语构词，同一后缀加在名词与动词上表现不同。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native English and the suffix reached English through Latin; the deep knowing root has Indo-European relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是英语本族，后缀经拉丁语进入英语；深层的「知」词根有印欧同族。

items.example: With nouns it describes a quality rather than a possibility.
items.exampleCN: 与名词结合时，它描述性质而非可能性。

items.example: The outcome is knowable in advance.
The rare negative form appears in reviews.
items.exampleCN: 这一罕用否定形式见于评论。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be; having the quality

definition_zh: 基本运算能力；数字素养；在日常与统计情境中运用数字的能力
definition_en: the ability to understand and work with numbers, especially in everyday and statistical contexts
core_image: 菜市场里，老人把三样菜钱心算加起来，比手机还快
scene: 菜市场里，老人用心算把三样菜钱加起来，比手机还快。Her numeracy was sharp enough to total the shopping before the app loaded.
sceneCN: 这里 numeracy 指「在日常生活里运用数字进行计算与判断的能力」（第 1 个义项：基本数字能力）；句意为她的数字能力足够强，在手机程序加载完之前就把账算好了。可辨识物件：菜摊、秤、零钱、手提袋。

pos.zh: 基本运算能力；数字素养；在日常与统计情境中运用数字的能力

senses.title: Basic ability with numbers
senses.definition: the ability to carry out simple arithmetic and make sense of quantities
senses.definitionCN: 进行简单运算并理解数量的能力
senses.example: Her numeracy was sharp enough to total the shopping before the app loaded.
senses.exampleCN: 她的数字能力足够强，在程序加载完之前就把账算好了。
senses.why: The word was built by analogy with literacy, so it names a basic competence rather than advanced mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是仿照「读写能力」造出的，因此命名的是基础能力，而非高等数学。

senses.title: School arithmetic competence
senses.definition: the arithmetic and measurement skills a school expects pupils to master
senses.definitionCN: 学校期望学生掌握的算术与测量技能
senses.example: Numeracy is assessed at the end of the primary years.
senses.exampleCN: 小学结束时会评估运算能力。
senses.why: Schools needed a single word for the arithmetic half of the basic curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 学校需要用一个词来指基础课程中算术那一半。

senses.title: Everyday adult numeracy
senses.definition: the practical number sense adults need for money, timetables and measurements
senses.definitionCN: 成人为处理金钱、时刻表与量度所需的实用数字感
senses.example: Adult numeracy classes fill up before the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 成人数字能力课在入冬前就报满了。
senses.why: The concept grew from concern about adults who could read but not handle figures.
senses.whyCN: 这一概念源于对「能读却不能算」的成人的关注。

senses.title: Quantitative literacy
senses.definition: the ability to read data, graphs and statistical claims critically
senses.definitionCN: 批判性地阅读数据、图表与统计主张的能力
senses.example: Numeracy now includes interpreting a risk figure in the news.
senses.exampleCN: 数字素养如今包括解读新闻里的风险数字。
senses.why: As public life filled with statistics, the word widened from sums to data judgement.
senses.whyCN: 随着公共生活充满统计，这个词从算数扩展到数据判断。

senses.title: Numeracy across subjects
senses.definition: the use of number skills inside science, geography and other lessons
senses.definitionCN: 在科学、地理等课程中使用数字技能
senses.example: The school runs numeracy across the curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校推行跨课程的数字素养。
senses.why: If number sense belongs everywhere, it cannot be confined to the mathematics room.
senses.whyCN: 若数字感处处都用得上，就不能把它关在数学教室里。

senses.title: Measuring numeracy
senses.definition: the testing and scoring of number skills for individuals or populations
senses.definitionCN: 对个人或人群数字技能进行测试与评分
senses.example: The survey compared numeracy scores across regions.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查比较了各地区的数字能力得分。
senses.why: A skill that matters to policy must be measured, and the word follows it into testing.
senses.whyCN: 对政策重要的技能必须被测量，这个词也跟着进入测评。

senses.title: A policy goal
senses.definition: a level of number competence that governments set and fund
senses.definitionCN: 政府设定并出资达成的数字能力水平
senses.example: Numeracy targets were added to the national plan.
senses.exampleCN: 数字能力目标被写进国家规划。
senses.why: Once governments fund it, numeracy becomes a target rather than a private accomplishment.
senses.whyCN: 一旦政府出资，数字能力就成了指标，而非个人的成就。

senses.title: The partner of literacy
senses.titleCN: 与读写能力并列的一项
senses.definition: the number counterpart to reading and writing in discussions of basic skills
senses.definitionCN: 在基础技能讨论中与读写作并列的数字对应项
senses.example: Employers ask for both literacy and numeracy.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主既要求读写能力，也要求数字能力。
senses.why: The word exists mainly because literacy had no counterpart, which is why the pair is so stable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词存在的主要原因是「读写」缺少对应项，所以这一对说法十分稳定。

intro.en: Numeracy is a twentieth-century coinage formed on literacy, with a Latin stem meaning 'number'. The date is well documented.
intro.cn: numeracy 是二十世纪仿照「读写能力」造出的词，词干来自表示「数」的拉丁语。年代有明确记录。

items.en: Numerus meant 'number, quantity, a count', and it supplies the stem of the word.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词意为「数、数量、计数」，为这个词提供词干。

items.en: The ending was copied from literacy, replacing the reading stem with the number stem, so the two words rhyme in shape.
items.cn: 词尾仿照「读写能力」复制而来，把阅读词干换成了数字词干，两个词因此结构相称。

items.en: The word is generally credited to a British report on education published in 1959, which needed a term for number competence.
items.cn: 这个词一般归功于一九五九年一份英国教育报告，该报告需要一个指数字能力的术语。

items.en: From the 1980s the term entered school inspection, adult education and international surveys of skills.
items.cn: 从一九八零年代起，该术语进入学校督导、成人教育与国际技能调查。

items.en: Recent use extends it to statistics and data literacy, well beyond mental arithmetic.
items.cn: 近来的用法把它扩展到统计与数据素养，远超心算范围。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attribution): the report popularised the term, but whether it coined it or borrowed it is not fully settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首创归属）：该报告使这个术语流行，但它是首创还是借用，尚无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin stem for number; group two holds the subjects and abilities numeracy is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁语「数」词干的词；第二组是拿来与数字素养比较的学科与能力。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'able to work with numbers'; numeracy is the noun for that ability.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「会算的」；numeracy 是表示这种能力的名词。

entries.definition: Meaning 'expressed in or involving numbers', a property of data rather than of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以数字表示的、涉及数字的」，是数据的性质，而非人的能力。

entries.definition: To list items one by one; it shares the number stem but means counting through a list.
entries.definitionCN: 逐项列出；同出「数」词干，但意为按清单逐个数过。

entries.definition: Meaning 'many', built on the same stem; it describes quantity, not competence.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「众多的」，同出该词干；它描述数量，而非能力。

entries.definition: The branch of mathematics dealing with the four operations; numeracy is the ability to use them in life.
entries.definitionCN: 研究四则运算的数学分支；数字素养是在生活中运用它们的能力。

entries.definition: A fuller term for numeracy used in research, stressing data and reasoning rather than sums.
entries.definitionCN: 研究中更完整的同义说法，强调数据与推理而非算数。

entries.definition: The whole field of number, shape and proof; numeracy is only its everyday floor.
entries.definitionCN: 关于数、形与证明的整个学科；数字素养只是它的日常底层。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write, the word on which numeracy was modelled.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力，正是数字素养所仿照的那个词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the number stem, the literacy model, and the school phrases that carry the term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「数」词干、「读写能力」这一模板，以及承载该术语的学校说法。

normal.en: Numeracy is to numbers what literacy is to letters; the two words were built to match.
normal.cn: 数字素养对数字的关系，正如读写能力对文字的关系；两个词是为对称而造的。

normal.en: The first syllable carries the Latin word for number, which also appears in numerical and enumerate.
normal.cn: 第一个音节带着拉丁语「数」，它也出现在表示「数值的」与「列举」的词中。

normal.en: School phrases show it is a basic skill: basic numeracy, numeracy test, adult numeracy.
normal.cn: 学校说法显示它是基础技能：基本运算能力、数字能力测试、成人数字素养。

normal.en: Numeracy is not advanced mathematics; it is the arithmetic a citizen needs at a till or a polling station.
normal.cn: 数字素养不是高等数学，而是公民在收银台或投票站需要的算数。

normal.en: People who lack it are called innumerate, a word built to mirror illiterate.
normal.cn: 缺乏这种能力的人被称为「不会算的」，这个词也是照着「不识字」造出的。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of coins counted without looking down.
abstract.cn: 想象一把硬币，不必低头就数清了。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe halved in the head while the hands keep chopping.
abstract.cn: 想象双手继续切菜，头脑里已把配方减半。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler held up to a shelf and the gap read at a glance.
abstract.cn: 想象把尺子搁在架子上，一眼读出差距。

examples.en: Numeracy is now tested alongside reading in most schools.
examples.cn: 多数学校现在把数字能力与阅读一起测试。

examples.en: Low numeracy makes loan offers hard to compare.
examples.cn: 数字能力低会让人难以比较贷款方案。

examples.en: The course builds numeracy through real shop receipts.
examples.cn: 这门课通过真实的购物小票培养数字能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「数得明白」——把数和账算得清楚 → 数字素养

root: 拉丁语「数、计数」加仿「读写能力」而造的英语词尾；英语 numeracy 指在日常与统计情境中运用数字的基础能力。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one basic competence: getting numbers right in real situations. It begins with sums, moves into school arithmetic, adult life, statistics, other subjects, testing, policy and finally its pairing with literacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一项基础能力展开：在真实情境中把数字弄对。它从算数开始，进入学校算术、成人生活、统计、其他课程、测评、政策，最后是与读写能力的并列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: coins counted correctly in the hand while a queue waits.
core.cn: 核心意象：排队的人还在等，手里的硬币已经数对了。

branches.en: THE FLOOR: simple sums and school arithmetic are the base layer the word was coined for.
branches.cn: 底层：简单算数与学校算术，正是造词时所指的基础层。

branches.en: THE ADULT TILL: money, timetables and measures turn the skill into daily survival.
branches.cn: 成人的收银台：金钱、时刻表与量度把这技能变成日常生存。

branches.en: THE STATISTICAL EYE: reading a risk figure is the modern extension of number sense.
branches.cn: 统计的眼光：读懂风险数字是数字感的现代延伸。

branches.en: EVERY ROOM: if number sense is needed in science and geography, it cannot belong to one subject.
branches.cn: 每间教室：若科学与地理都需要数字感，它就不能属于单一学科。

branches.en: MEASURED AND FUNDED: tests, targets and the pairing with literacy turn a skill into public policy.
branches.cn: 被测量与被出资：测试、指标与和读写能力的并列，把技能变成公共政策。

intro.en: Numeracy is a modern noun with a Latin stem and a borrowed ending; the endings it takes elsewhere are worth separating.
intro.cn: numeracy 是现代名词，拉丁词干加借来的词尾；它在别处所带的词尾值得分清。

latinIntro.en: The stem means 'number'. The English ending was copied from the word for reading and writing, which is why the pair sounds symmetrical.
latinIntro.cn: 词干意为「数」。英语词尾是从表示读写能力的词复制来的，所以这一对听起来对称。

items.example: The stem supplies the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供词的前半。

items.example: The ending makes a noun of ability.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成表示能力的名词。

items.meaning: the ability to work with numbers
items.example: Numeracy is taught from the first year.
items.exampleCN: 数字能力从一年级开始教。

items.example: A numerate citizen can check a bill.
items.exampleCN: 会算的公民能核对账单。
这个标签与「不识字」相对应。

definition_zh: 学术上；在学业方面；从学术角度看
definition_en: in relation to academic study, or in a way that concerns school and university learning
core_image: 公告栏把毕业生分成几档，最高一栏写着进入研究型大学的人数
scene: 县中学的公告栏上，毕业生被分成几档，最高一栏写着进入研究型大学的人数。She was academically strong but struggled in the workshop.
sceneCN: 这里 academically 指「在学业与学术表现方面」（第 1 个义项：就学业而言）；句意为她在学业上很强，但在车间里却吃力。可辨识物件：公告栏、排名表、红笔标记、车间工具。

pos.zh: 学术上；在学业方面；从学术角度看

senses.title: In terms of study
senses.definition: with respect to school or university learning rather than practical or social matters
senses.definitionCN: 就中小学或大学的学习而言，而非实务或社交方面
senses.example: She was academically strong but struggled in the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学业上很强，但在车间里却吃力。
senses.why: The adverb marks the domain being judged, so it sets study apart from other kinds of ability.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标出被评判的领域，从而把学业与其他能力区分开。

senses.title: Performing well in study
senses.definition: in a way that shows high achievement in academic subjects
senses.definitionCN: 在学科成绩上显出高水平
senses.example: The scholarship is awarded to academically outstanding students.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金颁给学业出众的学生。
senses.why: Achievement needs a measure, and the adverb supplies the academic yardstick.
senses.whyCN: 成绩需要一把尺，这个副词提供的正是学业这把尺。

senses.title: As a matter of school orientation
senses.definition: in a way that treats academic subjects as the main purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把学科学习当作主要目的的做法
senses.example: The school is academically oriented but weak in sport.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以学业为重，体育却薄弱。
senses.why: Institutions choose what to emphasise, and the adverb names the emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 学校会选择强调什么，这个副词命名的就是那种强调。

senses.title: By academic standards
senses.definition: judged against the rigour expected in scholarship
senses.definitionCN: 按照学术研究应有的严格程度来评判
senses.example: The programme is academically rigorous.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目学术要求严格。
senses.why: Standards differ by field, and the adverb anchors the judgement in academic expectations.
senses.whyCN: 标准因领域而异，这个副词把判断锚定在学术期待上。

senses.title: Recognised in academic terms
senses.definition: validated by scholarly criteria rather than commercial or popular ones
senses.definitionCN: 按学术标准而非商业或大众标准获得认可
senses.example: The qualification is academically recognised abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这一资格在国外获得学术承认。
senses.why: Recognition can come from several quarters, and the adverb says which one counts.
senses.whyCN: 认可可以来自多方，这个副词说明哪一方算数。

senses.title: At an academic disadvantage
senses.titleCN: 在学业条件上处于劣势
senses.definition: in a way that leaves a student behind in school learning
senses.definitionCN: 在学业学习上使学生处于落后状态
senses.example: Rural pupils were academically disadvantaged by the closures.
senses.exampleCN: 学校关闭使农村学生在学业上处于劣势。
senses.why: Gaps are measured in learning, so disadvantage is often described with this adverb.
senses.whyCN: 差距是以学习来衡量的，因此劣势常用这个副词来描述。

senses.title: Speaking academically
senses.definition: in the manner of academic discussion, with definitions and evidence
senses.definitionCN: 以学术讨论的方式，带定义与证据
senses.example: Academically speaking, the two terms are not interchangeable.
senses.exampleCN: 从学术角度说，这两个术语不能互换。
senses.why: The adverb can also frame a whole statement as scholarly rather than casual.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词也能把整句话框定为学术性的，而非随意的。

senses.title: Pursuing an academic path
senses.definition: in a direction that leads towards research and university teaching
senses.definitionCN: 朝着研究与大学教学发展的方向
senses.example: He was academically inclined from an early age.
senses.exampleCN: 他从小就偏向学术。
senses.why: A career choice can be academic, and the adverb describes the inclination.
senses.whyCN: 职业选择也可以是学术性的，这个副词描述的正是那种倾向。

intro.en: Academically is the adverb of academic, which descends from the name of Plato's school in Athens. The dates are approximate.
intro.cn: academically 是表示「学术的」那个形容词的副词形式，而该形容词源自雅典柏拉图学园的名字。年代均为约数。

items.en: The grove outside Athens where Plato taught was named after a local hero; the hero's own name is of uncertain origin and is marked as source uncertain.
items.cn: 柏拉图授课的雅典郊外园林以一位当地英雄命名；这位英雄名字本身的来源不确定，标为来源不确定。

items.en: Latin took the place name as a noun for the school and its followers, and the word kept the philosophical setting.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个地名用作名词，指该学园及其追随者，词义保留着哲学场景。

items.en: The adjective meant 'of the Academy', and it described both the place and the kind of discussion held there.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「学园的」，既描述地点，也描述在那里进行的那类讨论。

items.en: English adopted the adjective for things belonging to schools of higher learning, and later for scholarly subjects in general.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，指属于高等学府的事物，后来泛指学术科目。

items.en: Adding the ordinary adverb ending produced a word for judging something by academic standards.
items.cn: 加上普通的副词词尾，就得到按学术标准评判某事的词。

items.en: Source uncertain (hero's name): the origin of the name behind the place is not established, so any deeper etymology is a hypothesis rather than a result.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英雄之名）：该地名背后那个人名的来源未得证明，任何更深的词源都只是假说，而非结论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same school name; group two holds adverbs of learning that come from other roots.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一学园名称的形式；第二组是来自其他词根、表示学习的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective describes what belongs to study; the adverb describes how something is done or judged.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词描述属于学习的事物；副词描述某事如何被做或被评判。

entries.definition: The noun for the academic world; it names the place or community, not the manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指学术界的名词；它命名场所或群体，而非方式。

entries.definition: A school or learned society; the word keeps the original institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 学校或学术团体；这个词保留着原本的机构义。

entries.definition: From a Greek word for a teacher, but with a negative tone; it means in an overly bookish way.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语中表示教师的词，但带贬义；意为过于拘泥书本地。

entries.definition: In terms of the education system as a whole; it is broader than academically.
entries.definitionCN: 就整个教育制度而言；比 academically 更宽。

entries.definition: In relation to formal schooling and examinations; it sounds older and narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 就正式学校教育与考试而言；听起来更旧、更窄。

entries.definition: In terms of thinking and reasoning ability, whether or not a school is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 就思考与推理能力而言，未必涉及学校。

entries.definition: In terms of doing and use; it is the usual contrast to academically.
entries.definitionCN: 就动手与实际运用而言；常作为 academically 的对照。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the school name at the root, the adverb ending, and the practical contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词根里的学园名称、副词词尾，以及与实务的对照。

normal.en: The root is the name of Plato's school, so anything academically judged is judged by school standards.
normal.cn: 词根是柏拉图学园的名字，因此凡按 academically 评判的，都是按学校标准评判。

normal.en: The ending turns the adjective into a statement about how something is done or measured.
normal.cn: 词尾把形容词变成关于「如何做或如何衡量」的陈述。

normal.en: The usual contrast is practical: strong academically, weak in the workshop.
normal.cn: 最常见的对照是实务：学业强，车间里弱。

normal.en: School phrases carry it: academically gifted, academically oriented, academically disadvantaged.
normal.cn: 学校说法常带着它：学业有天赋、以学业为重、学业处于劣势。

normal.en: The whole Academy family shares the name: academic, academia, academy, academically.
normal.cn: 整个「学园」词族共享这个名字：学术的、学术界、学院、学术上。

abstract.en: Picture a report card read aloud while a toolbox sits untouched.
abstract.cn: 想象有人朗读成绩单，而工具箱一直没被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder leaning against a library shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子靠在图书馆的书架旁。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler marked in grades rather than in centimetres.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子刻的是成绩等级，而不是厘米。

examples.en: The two candidates were academically comparable.
examples.cn: 两位候选人在学业上相当。

examples.en: Academically, the argument is sound but the evidence is thin.
examples.cn: 从学术上说，论证成立，但证据薄弱。

examples.en: The programme is academically demanding and practically useful.
examples.cn: 这个项目学术要求高，也很实用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「学园里那一套」——按学校的标准来评 → 学术上

root: academic（学术的，源自雅典柏拉图学园的地名）+ 英语副词词尾；英语 academically 指在学业方面、按学术标准。该地名背后人名的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question: measured by which standard? The adverb keeps pointing to the school, from plain study through achievement, orientation, rigour, recognition, disadvantage, formal phrasing and career direction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：按哪把尺来衡量？这个副词始终指向学校，从单纯的学习，到成绩、办学方向、严格程度、认可、劣势、正式表述与职业方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked in grades instead of centimetres.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻着成绩等级而非厘米的尺子。

branches.en: THE DOMAIN: the adverb first marks that the judgement concerns study rather than life in general.
branches.cn: 领域：这个副词首先标出判断针对学习，而非一般生活。

branches.en: THE SCALE'S TWO ENDS: the same measure records high achievement and serious disadvantage.
branches.cn: 尺子的两端：同一把尺既记录优异成绩，也记录严重劣势。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION'S CHOICE: a school can emphasise academic work and set its rigour.
branches.cn: 学校的选择：学校可以强调学业，并设定其严格程度。

branches.en: THE STAMP: recognition by academic criteria is a seal from one particular authority.
branches.cn: 印章：按学术标准的认可，是某一个特定权威盖下的章。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND THE PATH: the adverb can frame a sentence or point a career towards research.
branches.cn: 框定与路径：这个副词既能框定一句话，也能把职业指向研究。

intro.en: Academically is a three-piece English word: a borrowed stem, an adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: academically 是三段式英语词：借来的词干、形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is the Greek place name as Latin took it; the endings are the ordinary English adjective and adverb endings.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语所取的希腊地名；词尾是普通的英语形容词与副词词尾。

items.structure: Akademeia (Greek place name, the grove of a hero)
items.example: The place name became the word for a school.
items.exampleCN: 这个地名成了表示学校的词。

items.structure: academia (Latin noun from the place name)
items.example: The noun keeps the institutional sense.
The style was attacked as academicism.
items.exampleCN: 这种风格被指为学院主义。

latinEntries.meaning: the Academy; a school of philosophy

definition_zh: 学术界；高校与科研机构的整体；学术生涯与研究文化
definition_en: the world of universities, research and scholarly work, considered as a community and a career
core_image: 一间会议厅，同一篇论文的作者名单比正文还长，来自六所大学
scene: 会议厅里，同一篇论文的作者名单比正文还长，来自六所大学。Academia rewards long author lists as much as clear findings.
sceneCN: 这里 academia 指「以高校与科研机构为主体的学术界」（第 1 个义项：学术共同体）；句意为学术界对冗长作者名单的奖励，不亚于对清晰结论的奖励。可辨识物件：会议厅、投影幕、作者名单、桌牌。

pos.zh: 学术界；高校与科研机构的整体；学术生涯与研究文化

senses.title: The academic community
senses.definition: the people who produce and transmit scholarly knowledge, taken as one world
senses.definitionCN: 把生产与传递学术知识的人看作一个整体世界
senses.example: Academia rewards long author lists as much as clear findings.
senses.exampleCN: 学术界对冗长作者名单的奖励，不亚于对清晰结论的奖励。
senses.why: The word names a society of scholars rather than a building or a single institution.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是学者的社会，而非一栋楼或一个机构。

senses.title: Universities as a whole
senses.definition: the universities and research institutes considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 把大学与科研机构合起来看
senses.example: Most of academia was closed for the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 假期里多数高校都关门了。
senses.why: When many institutions act alike, they can be spoken of as one body.
senses.whyCN: 当许多机构行动相同时，就可以被当作一个整体来说。

senses.title: An academic career
senses.definition: the working life of teaching and research inside universities
senses.definitionCN: 在大学内从事教学与研究的职业生涯
senses.example: She left industry for a life in academia.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开产业界，去过学术生涯。
senses.why: The word also names a career path, with its own hiring, promotion and insecurity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也命名一条职业路径，有自己的聘任、晋升与不稳定。

senses.title: The culture of research
senses.definition: the habits, incentives and hierarchies that shape how research is done
senses.definitionCN: 塑造研究如何进行的习惯、激励与等级
senses.example: Academia prizes novelty over replication.
senses.exampleCN: 学术界看重新颖，胜过重复验证。
senses.why: A community has customs, and the word often carries criticism of those customs.
senses.whyCN: 共同体有自己的习俗，这个词常带着对这些习俗的批评。

senses.title: Academic publishing
senses.definition: the journals, presses and review systems through which scholarship circulates
senses.definitionCN: 学术成果流通所依赖的期刊、出版社与评审制度
senses.example: Academia runs on unpaid reviewing.
senses.exampleCN: 学术出版靠无偿审稿运转。
senses.why: Publishing is the circulatory system of the scholarly world, so the word covers it too.
senses.whyCN: 出版是学术世界的循环系统，这个词也覆盖了它。

senses.title: Scholars across disciplines
senses.definition: the whole company of researchers, whatever their field
senses.definitionCN: 不论领域的全体研究者
senses.example: The question split academia along disciplinary lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题按学科界线把学者群体分成两派。
senses.why: The word unites fields that otherwise share little, which is why it is useful in public debate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把原本共享甚少的领域联合起来，因此在公共讨论中很有用。

senses.title: Academia against industry
senses.titleCN: 与产业界相对的学术界
senses.definition: the academic sector as a counterpart to business and government
senses.definitionCN: 作为商业与政府对应方的学术部门
senses.example: The technology moved from academia to industry in five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项技术在五年内从学术界转到产业界。
senses.why: Sectors define themselves by contrast, and this word is often used to mark one side of a divide.
senses.whyCN: 部门靠对照来定义自身，这个词常用来标记分界的一边。

senses.title: The original Academy
senses.definition: the philosophical school founded by Plato, from which the modern word descends
senses.definitionCN: 柏拉图创立的哲学学园，现代词义由此而来
senses.example: Academia began as a garden with a teacher in it.
senses.exampleCN: 学术界最初只是一座有教师的花园。
senses.why: The modern word keeps the memory of one school in Athens, named after a local hero.
senses.whyCN: 现代词义保留着雅典那所学园的记忆，它以一个当地英雄命名。

intro.en: Academia is the Latin form of the name of Plato's school; its use for the whole scholarly world is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: academia 是柏拉图学园名称的拉丁语形式；用它指整个学术界要晚得多。年代均为约数。

items.en: The garden outside Athens where Plato taught took its name from a local hero; the hero's name is of uncertain origin and marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 柏拉图授课的雅典郊外园林得名于一位当地英雄；这位英雄名字的来源不确定，标为来源不确定。

items.en: Latin used academia for the school and for the philosophical tradition that grew from it.
items.cn: 拉丁语用这个词指该学园以及由它生长出的哲学传统。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin noun, first for the ancient school and for academies of learned people.
items.cn: 英语借入这个拉丁名词，最初指古代学园与博学者的团体。

items.en: By the twentieth century it named the whole university sector, especially in contrast with industry and government.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，它指整个大学部门，尤用于与产业界和政府对照。

items.en: Source uncertain (hero's name and first date): the name behind the place is unexplained, and the shift to the general scholarly world cannot be dated precisely.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英雄之名与首见年代）：地名背后的人名无解释，转向泛指学术界的确切年代也无法确定。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same place name; group two holds words for the same world seen as a sector or a system.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一地名的形式；第二组是把同一个世界看成部门或制度的词。

entries.definition: A single school or learned society; academia is the whole world those institutions form.
entries.definitionCN: 单个学校或学术团体；academia 是这些机构构成的整个世界。

entries.definition: A literary shortening of the same word, used for the scholarly world with a slightly mocking tone.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的书面缩略形式，指学术界，略带嘲讽意味。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun for a person; academia names the setting those people share.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词及指人的名词；academia 命名这些人共处的场域。

entries.definition: Capitalised, it can name a specific historic school; the lower-case word is generic and institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 大写时可指某个特定的历史学园；小写时是泛指机构的词。

entries.definition: The organised system of universities and colleges, including funding and policy; academia stresses the people and culture.
entries.definitionCN: 由大学与学院构成的制度体系，含经费与政策；academia 更强调人与文化。

entries.definition: A neutral description of the same community, without the career and critique overtones.
entries.definitionCN: 对同一共同体的中性描述，不带职业与批评的意味。

entries.definition: The part of academia that produces new findings, excluding teaching-led work.
entries.definitionCN: 学术界中产出新发现的那部分，不含以教学为主的工作。

entries.definition: The universities viewed as a budget line and a policy area, a colder phrase than academia.
entries.definitionCN: 把大学看作预算项目与政策领域，比 academia 冷峻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the school name, the contrast with industry, and the institutions it contains.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：学园之名、与产业界的对照，以及它所包含的机构。

normal.en: The word is the Latin name of Plato's garden, reused for every garden of research since.
normal.cn: 这个词是柏拉图园林的拉丁名，后来被用于此后每一座研究园地。

normal.en: Academia is the world; an academy is one building inside it.
normal.cn: 学术界是那个世界；一所学院是其中的一栋楼。

normal.en: Public debate usually sets academia against industry or government.
normal.cn: 公共讨论通常把学术界与产业界或政府对立起来。

normal.en: In academia people speak of hiring, tenure and publishing, which are career words, not building words.
normal.cn: 在学术界，人们谈聘任、终身教职与发表，这些是职业词，不是建筑词。

normal.en: Academe is the shorter, older, slightly ironic version of the same idea.
normal.cn: 「学术圈」是同一想法更短、更旧、也略带反讽的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a garden with many gates and no single owner.
abstract.cn: 想象一座有许多门、却没有单一主人的花园。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are added by the readers.
abstract.cn: 想象一座书架由读者自己添置的图书馆。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor where every door leads to another corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长走廊，每扇门都通向另一条走廊。

examples.en: She moved between academia and government twice.
examples.cn: 她在学术界与政府之间来回换过两次。

examples.en: Academia is slow to change its hiring habits.
examples.cn: 学术界改变聘任习惯很慢。

examples.en: The discovery sat in academia for a decade before industry noticed.
examples.cn: 这项发现留在学术界十年，产业界才注意到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「学园那一圈」——围着学园转的一整个圈子 → 学术界

root: 雅典柏拉图学园名称的拉丁语形式，学园得名于一位当地英雄，该英雄名字来源不确定；英语 academia 指以高校与科研机构为主体的学术界。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one world: the people and institutions that produce scholarship. The world can be seen as a community, a sector, a career, a culture, a publishing system, a discipline-spanning crowd, one side of a divide, or the original garden it grew from.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述同一个世界：生产学术的人与机构。这个世界可以被看成共同体、部门、职业、文化、出版系统、跨学科的群体、分界的一边，或者它最初长出的那座园子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a garden full of scholars, with gates opening onto the rest of society.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座满是学者的园子，几道门通向社会其余部分。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the word starts as one garden with one teacher in Athens.
branches.cn: 源头：这个词起初只是雅典一座有一个教师的园子。

branches.en: THE COMPANY: scholars of every field form one community whether or not they share methods.
branches.cn: 共同体：各领域学者构成一个共同体，尽管方法未必相通。

branches.en: THE BUILDINGS: universities and institutes are the visible body of that community.
branches.cn: 建筑：大学与研究所是这个共同体的可见躯体。

branches.en: THE WORKING LIFE: hiring, promotion and daily habits turn the community into a career and a culture.
branches.cn: 职业生活：聘任、晋升与日常习惯把共同体变成职业与文化。

branches.en: THE CIRCULATION AND THE DIVIDE: publishing moves the work, and the contrast with industry marks the border.
branches.cn: 流通与分界：出版让成果流动，与产业界的对照则划出边界。

intro.en: Academia is a borrowed noun with almost no affix structure of its own; its family is built by adding endings to the same stem.
intro.cn: academia 是借来的名词，本身几乎没有词缀结构；它的词族靠在同一词干上加词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The stem is the Greek place name as Latin reshaped it; English builds academy, academic and academically from the same base.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语改写后的希腊地名；英语用同一基础构成学院、学术的与学术上。

items.meaning: the grove of the hero Akademos
items.meaningCN: 英雄阿卡德摩斯的园林
items.example: The place name is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个地名是整个词族的根。

items.structure: academia (Latin noun from the place name)
items.example: Academia now means the whole sector.
items.exampleCN: 这个词如今指整个学术部门。
该学会选出了十名成员。
这一届学生学业水平多样。
这一运动排斥学院主义。

items.meaning: a member of a learned academy

definition_zh: 奖学金；学术研究，学问；学术成果的整体；学识
definition_en: money awarded to a student to support study, or the serious academic work and learning of a field
core_image: 系办公室墙上贴着一张名单，获奖者免交学费，每月还领到生活费
scene: 系办公室的墙上贴着一张名单，获奖者免交学费，还每月领到生活费。The scholarship covered her tuition and a small monthly stipend.
sceneCN: 这里 scholarship 指「发给学生、用于支持学业的奖学金」（第 1 个义项：奖学金）；句意为这项奖学金覆盖了她的学费，还每月给她一小笔生活费。可辨识物件：名单、办公室门、学费单、信封。

pos.zh: 奖学金；学术研究，学问；学术成果的整体；学识

collocations.zh: 关于该主题的研究文献

derivatives.zh: 经院哲学的；学校教育的

senses.title: Money for study
senses.definition: a sum awarded to a student to pay for tuition, fees or living costs
senses.definitionCN: 发给学生、用于支付学费或生活费的一笔钱
senses.example: The scholarship covered her tuition and a small monthly stipend.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金覆盖了她的学费，还每月给她一小笔生活费。
senses.why: The suffix means 'condition or office', so a scholarship was first the state of being a scholar, then the support that made it possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀表示「身份或职位」，因此这个词先指学者的身份，再指使这一身份成为可能的资助。

senses.title: Serious academic work
senses.definition: the careful, systematic study of a subject by recognised methods
senses.definitionCN: 按公认方法对某一主题进行的细致系统研究
senses.example: Her scholarship on the archive took twelve years.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这批档案的研究做了十二年。
senses.why: The uncountable sense names the activity itself, not the money that supports it.
senses.whyCN: 不可数义命名活动本身，而非支持它的钱。

senses.title: The body of published work
senses.titleCN: 已发表的学术成果整体
senses.definition: the accumulated research and writing on a topic
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一主题积累起来的研究与写作
senses.example: The new book sums up forty years of scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 这本新书总结了四十年的研究成果。
senses.why: A topic accumulates a literature, and the word names that literature as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 一个主题会积累出文献，这个词整体地命名那些文献。

senses.title: Academic achievement
senses.definition: the level of learning a person has reached through study
senses.definitionCN: 一个人通过学习达到的学识水平
senses.example: The prize recognises scholarship rather than popularity.
senses.exampleCN: 该奖项表彰的是学术造诣，而非人气。
senses.why: The older sense measured the person's depth, not the institution's output.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的义项衡量个人的深度，而非机构的产出。

senses.title: The position of a scholar
senses.definition: the status or tenure of a student holding an award, or of a scholar in a college
senses.definitionCN: 获得资助的学生身份，或在学院中作为学者的职位
senses.example: The college attached a scholarship to the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学院把这个房间配给一项学籍。
senses.why: The sense comes from the older meaning of a scholar as a member of a college with a place and a income.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自较旧的用法：学者是学院中有一席之地与一份收入的人。

senses.title: A scholarship examination
senses.definition: the competitive test by which awards are allocated
senses.definitionCN: 用来分配奖助学金的竞争性考试
senses.example: She sat the scholarship at eleven and won it.
senses.exampleCN: 她十一岁参加奖学金考试并获了奖。
senses.why: Where money is scarce, a test decides who receives it, and the word transfers to the test.
senses.whyCN: 钱少的地方靠考试决定谁获得，这个词因此转指考试。

senses.title: Learning in a field
senses.definition: deep familiarity with a discipline's sources and debates
senses.definitionCN: 对某一学科原始材料与争论的深入熟悉
senses.example: The lecture displayed real scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座显出真正的学问。
senses.why: A person can carry scholarship without publishing, which is why the word also describes mastery.
senses.whyCN: 一个人可以不发表而拥有学问，所以这个词也描述精通。

senses.title: Older sense of attainments
senses.definition: the older use for the learning a scholar has acquired, often contrasted with mere information
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指学者所获得的学识，常与单纯的信息相对
senses.example: The obituary praised his scholarship and his modesty.
senses.exampleCN: 讣告称赞他的学识与谦逊。
senses.why: Before grants existed, the word meant what a scholar had become, not what a scholar had won.
senses.whyCN: 在资助制度出现之前，这个词指学者成为什么样的人，而非赢得了什么。

intro.en: Scholarship is scholar plus the native suffix -ship, which marks a state or an office. Scholar itself goes back through Latin to a Greek word for leisure. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: scholarship 是表示「学者」的名词加本族后缀，该后缀标记状态或职位。scholar 本身经拉丁语可追溯到希腊语中表示「闲暇」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Skholē meant 'leisure, free time, and then a discussion held in that time', from which the sense 'school' grew.
items.cn: 这个希腊词意为「闲暇、空余时间，进而指在闲暇中进行的讨论」，由此生长出「学校」的意思。

items.en: Latin schola took the Greek word for a place of lecture and study, and from it came scholaris 'of a school'.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊词，指讲学与读书的场所，并由它构成表示「学校的」形容词。

items.en: English scholar first meant a pupil or a learned person, and the two senses have coexisted for centuries.
items.cn: 这个词最初指学生或博学之人，这两个义项并存了数百年。

items.en: The native suffix marks a condition or an office, as in friendship or membership, so scholarship first meant the scholar's state.
items.cn: 这个本族后缀标记状态或职位，如友谊或会员身份，因此这个词最初指学者的状态。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word also named the endowment that supports a student, and that sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词也指资助学生的基金，这一义项如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest citations for the money sense are not firm, and the pre-Greek origin of the leisure word is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：资助义的最早书证不确，那个表示「闲暇」的词在希腊语之前的来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same school stock; group two holds the awards and the learning it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「学校」词干的词；第二组是易与之混淆的奖助项目与学问。

entries.definition: The person who studies; scholarship is the money, the work or the body of results.
entries.definitionCN: 做研究的人；scholarship 是钱、工作或成果整体。

entries.definition: Describes work done with care and evidence; it says nothing about money.
entries.definitionCN: 描述有据而严谨的工作；与钱无关。

entries.definition: Relating to schools and formal teaching, and historically to medieval theology; it is not the modern research sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与学校及正式教学有关，历史上也指中世纪神学；不是现代的研究义。

entries.definition: The institution from which the whole family comes; it names a place, not an award.
entries.definitionCN: 整个词族所出自的机构；它命名场所，而非奖助。

entries.definition: Funds given for a project, often to a researcher rather than a student; broader than a scholarship.
entries.definitionCN: 为项目提供的经费，常给研究者而非学生；比奖学金更宽。

entries.definition: A stipend for advanced study that often includes a community of fellows; it carries more prestige and longer terms.
entries.definitionCN: 支持高等研究的津贴，常附带研究员群体；声望更高、期限更长。

entries.definition: A small award given on financial need rather than merit, common in British institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 按经济需要而非成绩发放的小额资助，常见于英国院校。

entries.definition: Knowledge acquired by study; scholarship stresses method, evidence and contribution to a field.
entries.definitionCN: 通过学习获得的知识；scholarship 强调方法、证据与对领域的贡献。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the suffix of state, the two modern senses, and the awards it is compared with.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示状态的后缀、两个现代义，以及拿来比较的奖助项目。

normal.en: The ending means 'state or office', so scholarship began as the condition of being a scholar.
normal.cn: 词尾意为「状态或职位」，所以这个词最初指身为学者的状态。

normal.en: The same word covers the money and the work, which is why a sentence can be ambiguous without context.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指钱也指工作，所以脱离语境时句子可能含混。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate them: win a scholarship, a body of scholarship, scholarship on the topic.
normal.cn: 固定说法把它们分开：获得奖学金、一批学术成果、关于该主题的研究。

normal.en: A grant funds a project, a fellowship funds a person for longer, a bursary responds to need.
normal.cn: 经费资助项目，研究员津贴较长期地资助个人，助学金则回应经济需要。

normal.en: Scholar, scholarly, scholastic and school all descend from one Greek word for leisure.
normal.cn: 学者、治学的、经院式的与学校，都源自同一个表示「闲暇」的希腊词。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope that pays for years of quiet reading.
abstract.cn: 想象一个信封，为多年的安静阅读付账。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf that grows in depth rather than in height.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架向深处增长，而不是向高处增长。

abstract.en: Picture a long conversation carried on across centuries by footnotes.
abstract.cn: 想象一场靠脚注延续数百年的长谈。

examples.en: The scholarship is renewable if grades hold.
examples.cn: 成绩达标的话，这项奖学金可以续发。

examples.en: Recent scholarship has questioned the date of the letter.
examples.cn: 近期研究对该信件的年代提出质疑。

examples.en: Her scholarship is admired for its patience with sources.
examples.cn: 她的治学因对原始材料的耐心而受推重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「学者的那份」——给学者的资助，也是学者的本事 → 奖学金、学问

root: scholar（学者，经拉丁语来自希腊语「闲暇、讲学之处」）+ 表示状态或职位的本族后缀；英语 scholarship 指奖学金，也指学术研究与学问。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one scholar's life: the money that pays for it, the work itself, the literature it adds to, the depth it reaches, the status it confers, the test that opens it, the mastery it shows and the older praise for attainments.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一位学者的一生展开：为其付账的钱、工作本身、它所增添的文献、所达到的深度、所赋予的身份、开启它的考试、所显现的精通，以及旧时对造诣的称许。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an envelope of money beside a growing shelf of careful notes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装钱的信封，旁边是不断增厚的严谨笔记。

branches.en: THE SUPPORT: money, the status it buys and the test that allocates it belong to one machinery.
branches.cn: 资助机制：钱、钱所买的身份，以及分配它的考试，同属一套机器。

branches.en: THE WORK: careful systematic study is the sense that the money exists to make possible.
branches.cn: 工作：细致系统的研究，正是钱存在所要促成的那个义项。

branches.en: THE SHELF: a topic accumulates literature, and the word names the accumulation.
branches.cn: 书架：一个主题积累文献，这个词命名那份积累。

branches.en: DEPTH: achievement and mastery describe what a person has become, not what a person has won.
branches.cn: 深度：造诣与精通描述一个人成为什么，而非赢得什么。

branches.en: THE OLD PRAISE: before grants, the word measured a scholar's attainments alone.
branches.cn: 旧时的称许：在资助制度之前，这个词只衡量学者的造诣。

intro.en: Scholarship is a native suffix on a borrowed noun; separating the two halves explains both modern senses.
intro.cn: scholarship 是借来的名词加本族后缀；把两半分开，就能解释两个现代义。

latinIntro.en: The noun goes back through Latin to Greek, while the suffix is native English and marks a state or an office.
latinIntro.cn: 名词经拉丁语追溯到希腊语，而后缀是英语本族，标记状态或职位。

items.example: The scholar worked from primary sources.
items.exampleCN: 这位学者依据原始材料工作。

items.example: The suffix also appears in friendship.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾也出现在 friendship 中。

items.meaning: the scholar's state; support for study
in the manner of a scholar

这所学校建于一五四零年。

items.meaning: a student who holds an award
items.example: Every scholarship holder attends the dinner.
items.exampleCN: 每位奖学金获得者都参加晚宴。

latinEntries.meaning: a school; a place of lecture

definition_zh: 学者；研究者；（旧）学生，小学生；奖学金获得者；古典学者
definition_en: a person who studies a subject deeply and knows it well, especially through reading and research
core_image: 档案室里，一位研究者用放大镜辨认褪色的边注，把被涂掉的日期改了回来
scene: 档案室里，一位研究者用放大镜辨认褪色的边注，把日期改了回来。A scholar of medieval handwriting restored the erased date.
sceneCN: 这里 scholar 指「对某一学问领域做深入研究的人」（第 1 个义项：学者）；句意为一位研究中世纪笔迹的学者把被擦掉的日期复原了。可辨识物件：档案盒、放大镜、羊皮纸、铅笔。

pos.zh: 学者；研究者；（旧）学生，小学生；奖学金获得者

senses.title: A learned researcher
senses.definition: a person who has studied a subject deeply and contributes to knowledge about it
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题深有研究并为相关知识作出贡献的人
senses.example: A scholar of medieval handwriting restored the erased date.
senses.exampleCN: 一位研究中世纪笔迹的学者把被擦掉的日期复原了。
senses.why: The word began as a name for a person of study, and depth of reading remains its core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指从事学习的人，博览深读始终是它的核心。

senses.title: A student, especially a child
senses.definition: the older and still occasional use for a pupil at school
senses.definitionCN: 较旧、现今偶见的用法，指在校学生
senses.example: The head teacher addressed the scholars of the upper form.
senses.exampleCN: 校长对高年级的学生讲话。
senses.why: In older English any learner was a scholar, and schools still use the word in this formal way.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的英语里，任何学习者都是 scholar，学校至今仍以这种正式方式用它。

senses.title: A specialist in a field
senses.definition: an expert in one discipline, identified by the field after 'of'
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科的专家，用「研究……」引出领域
senses.example: She is a scholar of early Chinese astronomy.
senses.exampleCN: 她是研究中国古代天文学的学者。
senses.why: Specialisation narrows the general word to one discipline at a time.
senses.whyCN: 专业化把这一通称收窄到一次一个学科。

senses.title: A classical scholar
senses.definition: a person trained in Greek and Latin texts and their interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 受训于希腊拉丁文本及其解释的人
senses.example: The classical scholar corrected the quotation.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古典学者更正了引文。
senses.why: For centuries the deepest study meant Greek and Latin, so the word took that specific colour.
senses.whyCN: 数百年间最深的学问指希腊拉丁，这个词因此带上那层特定色彩。

senses.title: A scholarship holder
senses.definition: a student who holds an award, especially in older British usage
senses.definitionCN: 持有奖助的学生，尤用于较旧的英式说法
senses.example: The scholars dined together once a term.
senses.exampleCN: 奖学金获得者每学期聚餐一次。
senses.why: The institution's money and the person's learning once shared a single label.
senses.whyCN: 机构的钱与个人的学问曾共用一个标签。

senses.title: An independent scholar
senses.definition: a researcher working outside a university, often self-supporting
senses.definitionCN: 在大学之外工作的研究者，常自负经费
senses.example: Independent scholars rarely have access to the journal.
senses.exampleCN: 独立学者很少能访问该期刊。
senses.why: The word describes the activity, not the employer, which is why it can stand without a university.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述活动而非雇主，因此可以脱离大学而存在。

senses.title: A gentleman scholar
senses.definition: an old phrase for a leisured, well-read person without a professional post
senses.definitionCN: 旧时说法，指有闲暇、博览群书而无专职的人
senses.example: The gentleman scholar kept a private library.
senses.exampleCN: 这位博学之士有一间私人藏书室。
senses.why: The phrase marks a scholar who needed no salary, because leisure and private means made study possible.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法标记出不需要薪水的学者，因为闲暇与私产使治学成为可能。

senses.title: An archaic pupil
senses.definition: a very old use for a learner under a particular teacher
senses.definitionCN: 很旧的用法，指跟随某位教师学习的门徒
senses.example: The scholars of the old master copied his notes.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老先生的弟子抄录他的笔记。
senses.why: Before institutions, a scholar was simply someone who studied under a teacher.
senses.whyCN: 在机构出现之前，学者就是跟随某位教师学习的人。

intro.en: Scholar comes through Late Latin from Greek, where the source word meant 'leisure' and then 'a discussion held in leisure'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: scholar 经晚期拉丁语源自希腊语，源词意为「闲暇」，进而指「在闲暇中进行的讨论」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Skholē meant 'leisure, spare time, and the discussion that leisure allowed'; study was what free people did when work was done.
items.cn: 这个希腊词意为「闲暇、空余时间，以及闲暇所允许的讨论」；学习是自由人在劳作之余所做的事。

items.en: Latin schola shifted the word to the place and the group, a school, and from it formed scholaris 'of a school'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词转向场所与群体，即学校，并由它构成表示「学校的」形容词。

items.en: The Late Latin adjective was used as a noun for a member of a school, and that noun passed into English.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把这个形容词用作名词，指学校成员，这一名词传入了英语。

items.en: English adopted it early as scolere 'student', and the sense of a deeply learned person grew alongside it.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个词指「学生」，同时生长出「深有学问的人」这一义项。

items.en: Since the nineteenth century the word has chiefly meant a specialist researcher, often with the field named after 'of'.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，这个词主要指专门研究者，领域常用「研究……」引出。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek source of the leisure word is reconstructed, and the moment when 'pupil' gave way to 'researcher' is not dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：那个表示「闲暇」的词在希腊语之前的来源属重构形式，而「学生」让位于「研究者」的时点没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same school stock; group two holds the titles a scholar is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「学校」词干的词；第二组是拿来与学者比较的头衔。

entries.definition: Describes work that is careful and evidenced; a scholar is the person who does it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述有据而严谨的工作；学者是做这项工作的人。

entries.definition: The money, the research or the body of results; the scholar is the human agent behind all three.
entries.definitionCN: 钱、研究或成果整体；学者是这三者背后的人。

entries.definition: Relating to schools and medieval theology; it can sound pedantic where scholar sounds professional.
entries.definitionCN: 与学校及中世纪神学有关；在 scholar 显得专业的场合，它可能显得迂执。

entries.definition: The institution that gave the family its name; a scholar is a person shaped by it.
entries.definitionCN: 为整个词族提供名称的机构；学者是受它塑造的人。

entries.definition: A person who works in a university; a scholar may work outside one and is defined by depth of study.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学工作的人；学者可能在校外工作，并以研究深度来定义。

entries.definition: Someone who conducts systematic inquiry, often on funded projects; the word stresses method over learning.
entries.definitionCN: 从事系统探究的人，常依托资助项目；这个词强调方法而非学识。

entries.definition: A person enrolled in a course; the older sense of scholar overlapped with this, but the modern word does not.
entries.definitionCN: 注册在课程中的人；学者一词的旧义曾与之重叠，现代义则不然。

entries.definition: Someone with recognised skill in a practical field; scholarship implies reading and argument, not only technique.
entries.definitionCN: 在实务领域有公认技能的人；学者身份含阅读与论证，不只是技术。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the leisure root, the old pupil sense, and the field phrase with 'of'.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「闲暇」词根、旧的学生义，以及带「研究……」的领域说法。

normal.en: The root means leisure, because study was once what free time was for.
normal.cn: 词根意为闲暇，因为学习曾经就是空闲时间的用途。

normal.en: The same family gives school, scholarship, scholarly and scholastic, one root with four directions.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出学校、奖学金、治学的与经院式的，一个词根四个方向。

normal.en: The modern pattern is 'a scholar of' plus a field, which is how the word becomes specific.
normal.cn: 现代搭配是「研究某领域的学者」，这个词借此变得具体。

normal.en: In older British usage scholars are pupils, which is why school prize lists still say scholars.
normal.cn: 在较旧的英式用法里，学者就是学生，所以学校获奖名单仍写「学子」。

normal.en: A scholar can be independent, visiting or classical; the adjective before the noun says the setting or the field.
normal.cn: 学者可以是独立的、访问的或古典的；前面的形容词说明场景或领域。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass held over a page nobody else has read.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜对着一页别人没读过的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a chair at a desk that stays warm long after the room empties.
abstract.cn: 想象房间空了以后，书桌前那把椅子还留着温度。

abstract.en: Picture a footnote that argues with a book written centuries earlier.
abstract.cn: 想象一条脚注在与数百年前写成的一本书争论。

examples.en: The scholar spent a decade on one chapter.
examples.cn: 这位学者用十年写一章。

examples.en: She became a scholar of the region's oral poetry.
examples.cn: 她成了研究该地区口头诗歌的学者。

examples.en: Visiting scholars must apply for library access.
examples.cn: 访问学者须申请图书馆权限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有空就读书的人」——闲暇都用来读书 → 学者

root: 晚期拉丁语「学校成员」，源头为拉丁语「学校」，再往上为希腊语「闲暇、讲学之所」；英语 scholar 指深入研究某一学问的人，旧义指学生。更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person: someone who studies. The person can be a deep researcher, a school pupil, a field specialist, a classicist, an award holder, an independent worker, a leisured gentleman or an old master's follower.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指同一种人：做学问的人。这个人可以是深入研究的研究者、在校学生、某领域专家、古典学者、奖学金获得者、独立研究者、有闲暇的博学之士，或旧时某位先生的弟子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reader bent over a page with a magnifying glass, finding what others missed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位读者俯身用放大镜看一页纸，发现了别人漏掉的东西。

branches.en: THE READER: deep study in general and study of one named field are the same act at different widths.
branches.cn: 读者：泛泛的深读与对某一具名领域的深读，是同一动作的不同宽度。

branches.en: THE PUPIL: the oldest senses place the person inside a school or under a master.
branches.cn: 学生：最旧的义项把人放在学校里或某位先生门下。

branches.en: THE CLASSICIST: for centuries the deepest reading meant Greek and Latin texts.
branches.cn: 古典学者：数百年间最深的阅读意味着希腊拉丁文本。

branches.en: THE AWARD: institutional money once shared the name with the person who earned it.
branches.cn: 奖助：机构的钱曾与凭它受助的人共用一名。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE WALLS: independence and leisure both describe scholars who owe no salary to a university.
branches.cn: 墙外：独立与闲暇都描述不依赖大学薪水的学者。

intro.en: Scholar is a borrowed noun with a short English family; its endings mark the person, the work and the adjective.
intro.cn: scholar 是借来的名词，英语词族不长；其词尾分别标记人、工作与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The stem meant 'of a school'. English added its own endings to make the abstract noun, the adjective and the verbless variants.
latinIntro.cn: 词干意为「学校的」。英语加上本族词尾，构成抽象名词、形容词与无动词的变体。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是整个词族的基础。

items.meaning: of a school; a school member
items.example: The adjective became a noun for the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词变成了指人的名词。
这位学者读了那份手稿。

items.meaning: in the manner of a scholar
a student who also competes in sport
items.example: The scholar-athlete kept a full schedule.
items.exampleCN: 这位学生运动员日程排得很满。
